doc.title: Jim Cullum interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2007

chapter: Growing up and learning to play
title: Teaching himself cornet and finding the blues
summary: With a one-dollar method book and his father's help he learned a scale, found the blue note, and wanted to play blues like Armstrong.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: I see. Did you get a case with it?

It did have a funny little case. A funny little case. A little, almost like it was made out of paper the little case, it folded over. It was about this long, the whole business, and had a hole in it, wouldn’t play. I had to put adhesive tape over the hole. But and then I went later I bought a book, How to Play the Cornet, for one dollar. I had an eight dollar investment in this whole deal.
Well considering what you were probably making per hour, you know.

Yeah. I was making seventy-five cents. But anyway then in the book it had a chromatic scale which is every note going up, like every black and white key on the piano. And so at this point my father comes in and I’m showing him this stuff and he says it’s really interesting. So he took a pencil and circled the notes to make a diatonic scale, which is [scats], that’s a diatonic scale. And so I saw the fingerings for a diatonic scale and I started out. And so the first day I got that down. I could play that in one day. So the next © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -7-
day I figured I’d play a little song. I go with the cornet [scats] and then I figured out to go [scats]. A blue note see.
So once I hit that blue note, that was it, it was blues.
And I wanted to be a blues player, that was all I cared about, to play the blues, that’s all I wanted to do was play the blues, like Louis Armstrong.
That’s an important moment, that you could even hear that thing and go for it.

Yeah, and on the second day. So that was, and then I had all this music in my head and it was so hard to get all that to come through that brass instrument. Difficult. So my whole life has been trying to fulfill that.
